title: Stupid
text:
Dear Google Photos Team,

I’m genuinely frustrated with how Google Photos works on iPhone.

I use Google Photos specifically because I want my Google Photos library to remain separate from my iPhone’s Apple Photos library. I do NOT want Google Photos to automatically access, mix, or back up the photos currently stored on my iPhone.

I’m completely fine with Google Photos having access to the photos that are already stored in my Google account. What I’m NOT fine with is having to give the Google Photos app Full Access to my iPhone Photos library just to properly view my existing Google Photos library.

This creates a ridiculous choice:

* Give Google Photos Full Access → risk my iPhone photos being backed up/mixed into Google Photos and consuming my Google storage.
* Give Google Photos Limited Access → the app becomes frustratingly limited and doesn’t properly show my existing Google Photos experience.

And then, once someone’s Google storage fills up because Photos has backed up their iPhone library, Google starts warning that Gmail and other services may be affected unless they purchase additional storage.

Why can’t Google Photos simply let me access my existing Google Photos cloud library without requiring access to my entire Apple Photos library?

I should be able to say:

“Show me the photos already stored in my Google account. Do not access or back up anything from my iPhone unless I explicitly choose to upload it.”

That seems like a basic privacy and product-design requirement.

Please consider adding a clear option to use Google Photos on iPhone as a cloud-library-only app, completely separate from the Apple Photos library, with no requirement to grant Full Photos Access.

I love the concept of Google Photos, but this current experience makes me feel like I have to compromise my privacy just to access photos that are already mine and already stored in my Google account.

Please fix this.

Thanks.

title: Select All Option Needed
text:
I am a Google One Pro user and regularly back up large numbers of photos and videos. However, there is no proper “Select All” option when filtering specific types of files (for example, only videos or only photos). This makes managing and backing up large collections very time-consuming.

Please consider adding:
	1.	A true “Select All” option after applying filters (Photos / Videos / Date range).
	2.	A one-tap “Select All for Download” option to easily download everything when needed.
	3.	Better bulk management tools for users with large cloud storage plans.

Currently, selecting thousands of files manually is inefficient and frustrating, especially for paid users.

Additionally, the backup upload time estimate fluctuates heavily during large uploads. It would be helpful if upload speed reporting were more stable and transparent.

I hope these improvements can be considered in future updates.
